label: Companies House guidance · updated 1 June 2026
title: Companies House identity verification: what directors and PSCs must do
summary: Directors and people with significant control must verify their identity. Without it, a company cannot file its confirmation statement.
body:
Identity verification is now a legal requirement for anyone who sets up, runs, owns or controls a UK company. It is meant to stop people using companies for fraud and to make the Companies House register more reliable.

Who needs to verify

  • Directors, and their equivalents such as LLP members.
  • Directors of overseas companies registered in the UK.
  • People with significant control (PSCs).
  • Companies House authorised agents.

In most cases you verify once. Companies House will add other groups, such as people who file on a company's behalf, later.

How to verify

  • Yourself, free: through the 'Verify your identity for Companies House' service on GOV.UK One Login, using an app, online questions or a participating Post Office.
  • Through an authorised agent: an accountant or solicitor registered with Companies House as an Authorised Corporate Service Provider (ACSP) can verify you, from any country. They may charge a fee.

Once verified, you get a Companies House personal code. Keep it as safe as your tax reference.

When the code is needed

  • Existing directors: in the company's next confirmation statement. The company cannot file its confirmation statement unless all its directors are verified.
  • New directors: when they are appointed, or when the company is formed.
  • PSCs: through Companies House's PSC service, within a 14-day window.

What I would do

Check when your company's next confirmation statement is due and make sure every director has verified well before then. Acting as a director without verifying after the deadline can be an offence, and the company can be affected too. If you live abroad, the agent route is often the simplest.
